f30ff4d721.q: How does Viclarity help regulated firms connect compliance data across multiple tools and dashboards?
f30ff4d721.a: Organizations want more connectivity and quicker information across their systems. For example, when managing third-party vendors, users can see onboarding status, latest due diligence, data from external sources like CreditSafe or Experian, and have all components talk to each other and be presented centrally so organizations can gather information easily, readily, quickly and accurately across multiple solutions.

0609516490.q: What compliance challenges do healthcare and public sector organizations face compared to financial services?
0609516490.a: Healthcare and public sector organizations are heavily regulated with significant compliance and assurance requirements, often managed manually. Their regulatory inspections are paramount to continuing their business. However, they are less accustomed to technology in day-to-day operations compared to financial services workers. They face similar stakes—compliance failures can result in financial fines or license withdrawal—and they increasingly use compliance software to demonstrate audit trails and improve efficiency in collecting metrics and KPIs for governance reporting.

452fdf733d.q: How is Viclarity integrating AI into its RegTech platform without embedding it in the core product?
452fdf733d.a: Viclarity has added AI enhancements rather than embedding AI into the core workflow tool. They developed Reg Monitor for horizon scanning regulatory alerts, and an Insights feature that interrogates compliance data to identify areas of weakness or trends. They are also exploring AI agents to detect if complaints breach underlying regulations like the Consumer Protection Code, and provide gap analysis when new regulations emerge. These AI features are optional, giving clients comfort since they prefer not having AI heavily embedded in core products during the onboarding phase.

a35439ddd2.q: What will RegTech solutions and regulatory technology look like in three to five years?
a35439ddd2.a: RegTech will become more AI-driven and sophisticated, with incremental adoption of AI enhancements. Regulatory compliance burdens will likely remain as heavy or heavier, not lessen, making firm reliance on technology unavoidable. Expected developments include greater connectivity, more APIs linking to other systems, and streamlined collection methods for regulations like DORA. Boards and compliance teams will increasingly depend on RegTech solutions to demonstrate compliance more efficiently and effectively.

5dcbb9101b.q: How does Viclarity serve regulated industries beyond financial services such as insurance and healthcare?
5dcbb9101b.a: Viclarity is used by any regulated organization across a mixture of industries including healthcare, nursing home groups, public sector bodies, investment management firms, asset management firms, insurance companies, reinsurance companies, and mid-tier banks. For insurers, it tracks everything from marketing request sign-offs to subpoena workflows and manages regulatory data calls across federal and state-level obligations. The platform functions as a workflow and governance tool that helps these diverse sectors track compliance obligations, evidence them, and present results to boards and executives.
